1. **Make native ordering requirements conditional on the actual format.**

Inventing a sequence field or globally sorting records would be wrong.

   I would replace that instruction with:

   > Preserve the agent’s native ordering and branch-selection semantics. Use sequence numbers where provided, parent links for tree formats, and file order where the native format defines it. Test supported out-of-order cases.

   The instruction to treat everything outside known structural types as a result also needs qualification: an unfamiliar control record is not necessarily a tool result.

2. **Separate watcher invariants from architecture-specific techniques.**

   [The watcher section](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md:213) alternates between “never a polling ticker,” an expected reconciliation tick, and a required “safety-net poll.” The intended distinction is understandable, but the wording invites inconsistent implementations.

   I would say explicitly that filesystem events are the primary signal and bounded periodic reconciliation is permitted or required to recover missed events.

   Likewise, `WatchWindow*` should apply when the number of watched paths grows. Pi’s single-directory watch already keeps descriptor usage bounded; forcing rolling date windows would add machinery without addressing that problem.

3. **Specify startup-baseline and late-directory behavior with concrete examples.**

   “Emit nothing at startup” is clear as a goal, but the guide does not explain the registration/snapshot race that leads to Pi’s timestamp grace period.

   I would add acceptance cases for:
   
   - A file written just before startup: no emission.
   - A file changed while the initial watch is being established: eventual emission.
   - A newly adopted directory containing files with old preserved mtimes: emission.
   - An unchanged file at shutdown: no emission.

   These examples would make the [startup requirement](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md:216) substantially harder to satisfy accidentally with a weak test.

   [Honest data](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md:183) says `WorkspaceRoot` must never be empty, while an undetermined project must be “unknown.”

   The guide requires a native transcript derived from the parsed snapshot, while also requiring malformed and oversized records to be skipped. It does not say whether raw output includes malformed bytes, excluded records, or only accepted records.

Observations below come from its installed `session-manager.js`, tool declarations and implementations, and the [captured validation results](PI-VALIDATION.md).\n\n## Store and durable writes\n\nThe default store is `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/`. `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` replaces `~/.pi/agent`; `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` instead selects a flat directory shared by projects. A per-invocation `--session-dir` is not discoverable by this provider unless the override also identifies it.\n\nPi canonicalizes the local cwd, removes one leading slash or backslash, replaces remaining slashes, backslashes and colons with hyphens, and wraps the result in `--`. This encoding is lossy: project attribution must check the header's `cwd`. A recorded cwd can belong to another machine and is never canonicalized by the reader.\n\nFiles are named `<timestamp>_<session-id>.jsonl`, with colons and periods in the timestamp replaced by hyphens. Each JSONL file is the durable transcript for one session. Normal creation buffers the header, settings and initial user turn in memory until the first assistant message; Pi then writes the accumulated records and appends subsequent entries. A newly started conversation can therefore be absent from disk. Loading and migrating an existing file, branching into a new session, and file replacement must not be treated as ordinary append-only activity. The provider watches durable JSONL files directly, retaining only the active tree path for display. Nested extension/subagent files are outside its session-discovery depth.\n\nThere is no shared rolling transcript, checkpoint or lock file that this provider needs to read. Watch startup records existing files without publishing them; writes, late directory creation and replacement trigger bounded reconciliation. Shutdown drains callbacks and performs a final reconciliation.\n\n## Header and records\n\nThe first nonblank record is a header:\n\n```json\n{\"type\":\"session\",\"version\":3,\"id\":\"session-id\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-09-17T12:00:00.000Z\",\"cwd\":\"/project\"}\n```\n\n`version: 3` describes the file format, not the Pi application release. Normalized `Provider.Version` is therefore `unknown`. Normalized workspace selection is native `cwd`, then caller project, then process cwd; global enumeration leaves an absent native origin empty.\n\nSubsequent records have `type`, `id`, `parentId` (null at the root), and an ISO timestamp. Message records wrap a `message` object; native messages also carry epoch-millisecond timestamps. File order chooses the latest leaf; following `parentId` and reversing the resulting path gives the active conversation. Inactive branches remain in `RawData` but are not displayed. Cycles terminate the walk. Compaction markers preserve the earlier transcript rather than applying Pi's context-window truncation.\n\n| Entry type | Interpretation |\n| --- | --- |\n| `message` | User/assistant conversation or a tool result |\n| `model_change`, `thinking_level_change` | Runtime settings; assistant records carry their own model |\n| `compaction` | Render `summary` as a marker while retaining earlier turns |\n| `branch_summary` | Context about a branch the user left; not an active conversation turn |\n| `session_info` | User-visible session name; latest recorded value used in listing |\n| `label` | Tree-navigation metadata |\n| `custom`, `custom_message` | Extension state/injected context; retained raw, omitted from conversation |\n\nUnknown kinds and roles warn with file and physical line number. Valid envelopes remain in the tree so descendants do not lose their ancestors. Oversized and malformed body records warn and are skipped. A missing/invalid header prevents conversion. Accepted original record bytes supply normalized data, raw uploads and debug exports from one snapshot.\n\n## Messages\n\n- `user`: `content` is a string or an array of content blocks. Text is rendered; images remain in raw records.\n- `assistant`: `content` interleaves `text`, `thinking` and `toolCall` blocks. Tool calls have `id`, `name` and `arguments`. Normalization preserves this ordering, assigning distinct message IDs and carrying usage once per native assistant entry.\n- `toolResult`: `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `content`, optional `details`, and `isError`. Results merge into the matching call within the exchange. _**Agent (gpt-6-astra 2026-09-17 13:24:43Z)**_

**Internally, yes—but that distinction doesn’t reach the CLI.**

- Providers use [`spi.ClassifyCheckError`](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/check.go:13) to distinguish `not_found`, `permission_denied`, and other failures, primarily for diagnostics and analytics.
- [`CheckResult`](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/provider.go:13) only returns `Success`, `Version`, `Location`, and `ErrorMessage`. It doesn’t include the failure category.
- Consequently, [`checkAllProviders`](/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/check.go:209) prints ❌ for every unsuccessful result.

I’d add an `ErrorType` field to `CheckResult` and pass the existing classification through. The CLI could then display missing optional agents informationally while keeping actual failures prominent—without guessing from error-message text.

One wrinkle: several providers currently label **every binary-lookup error** as `not_found`. Those should use the shared classifier so permission problems aren’t accidentally softened.

No changes made.
